findings.reason: an implementer who adds only the named twenty-second constant fails the section's own churn done-when, and one who adds a two-minute cap adds a definition the section states it does not add.
findings.text: §2 describes the settle window as a supersession debounce ("a coordinator row followed by another transition of the same run within a twenty-second settle window prints only the later row") yet calls that twenty-second constant "the only definition §2 adds" (line 132) and asserts "the settle hold never keeps a row more than two minutes from its first transition" (line 133), a bound §5 gates on; a pure twenty-second supersession defers a run that changes state more often than every twenty seconds indefinitely, so the two-minute maximum is an unnamed second definition (a maximum hold) and the done-when case "a run changing state every ten seconds prints within two minutes of its first change" cannot be satisfied by the twenty-second window alone

findings.reason: §5's positive control asserts the observer-shown pane reproduces today's row count within 2%, so the plan must state whether the resolution change is shared or gated on the observer hold, or the control measures a pane that is not today's behaviour.
findings.text: §2 claims "a pane built with observer context shown keeps today's behaviour exactly ... which replay_row_policy uses for §5's comparison", but the same section's third exception rewrites the shared resolution rule ("a resolution row is dropped only when it completes an opener still held", lines 117–121), and that rule sits in `RowPolicy.feed` on the path an observer-shown pane also drives, so such a pane would print `blocked → completed_unpromoted` after a printed blocked where today `NOISE_RESOLUTIONS` drops it
